event.label: September 1332 (6 Edward III) — Oldest Ancestral Estate Record (694 Years Ago): "John le Lusshe — 12d" Taxed at Tisbury / Oakley Before the Black Death
event.desc: Pushes the documented Lusshe estate and surname horizon back 694 years into the early reign of King Edward III—sixteen years before the Black Death of 1348! Enrolled under Shaftesbury Abbey's manor of Tisbury just two lines below Alexander de Ocle (Oakley in Tisbury) and four lines above David de Seghulle (Sedgehill), taxpayer John le Lusshe (assessed 12d. on 15s. of surplus livestock/grain) captures both the Anglo-Norman 'le Lusshe' origin of the Lush surname and the exact Oakley-in-Tisbury farmstead strip still held by John Lusshe 148 years later in 1480.
event.note: [TNA E 179/196/8, Sept. 1332 Wiltshire Lay Subsidy (15th), Dunworth Hundred — Tisbury (Tysseburye), WRS Vol. 45, p. 44, col. 2] Alexander de Ocle — 20d | Walter Warner — 3s | John le Lusshe — 12d | Thomas de Toteredehulle — 4s | Edward le Wyke — 8s 10d | John Boterstake — 4s | David de Seghulle — 8s.
Verified verbatim on p. 44 of Crowley's Wiltshire Tax List of 1332 (the sole Lusshe household in all of 1332 Wiltshire); graded conservatively as Pre-Tudor Monastic Estate & Surname Continuity.
